subject: Financial Management
notes: Finance core. Numerical answers are stated in correctAnswer with working in explanation.

questions.text: The management of the acquisition and use of funds to maximise firm value is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management
questions.explanation: Financial management plans and controls the procurement and use of funds.

questions.text: The primary objective of financial management is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management
questions.explanation: Wealth maximisation increases the market value of shareholders equity.

questions.text: The three major decisions of financial management are investment financing and
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management
questions.explanation: Investment financing and dividend decisions form the core of finance.

questions.text: Profit maximisation and wealth maximisation always lead to the same decision
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management
questions.explanation: Profit maximisation ignores timing and risk while wealth maximisation accounts for both.

questions.text: Distinguish between profit maximisation and wealth maximisation
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management
questions.correctAnswer: Profit maximisation seeks short term accounting profit ignoring risk and timing while wealth maximisation seeks long term market value considering both.
questions.explanation: Wealth maximisation is the superior and more modern objective.

questions.text: Explain the functions of a financial manager
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management
questions.correctAnswer: The financial manager forecasts funds acquires finance allocates it to investments manages working capital and pays dividends while balancing risk and return.
questions.explanation: Cover fund raising allocation and the dividend decision.

questions.text: A rupee received today is worth more than a rupee received in future because of
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Time value of money and valuation
questions.explanation: Money today can be invested to earn interest so early receipt has value.

questions.text: The process of finding the present value of a future amount is called
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Time value of money and valuation
questions.explanation: Discounting converts a future value back to its present value.

questions.text: An annuity is a series of equal payments made at equal intervals
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Time value of money and valuation
questions.explanation: An annuity is a stream of equal periodic payments.

questions.text: Define compound interest
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Time value of money and valuation
questions.correctAnswer: Compound interest is interest earned on both the original principal and the interest accumulated in earlier periods.
questions.explanation: Compounding causes money to grow at an increasing rate.

questions.text: Explain the techniques of capital budgeting
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Techniques include traditional methods like payback and accounting rate of return and discounted methods like net present value and internal rate of return which consider the time value of money.
questions.explanation: Contrast traditional and discounted cash flow techniques.

questions.text: If 1000 is invested at ten percent compound interest for one year the amount is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Time value of money and valuation
questions.explanation: Amount equals principal times one plus rate so 1000 times 1.1 equals 1100.

questions.text: The process of evaluating and selecting long term investment projects is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.explanation: Capital budgeting evaluates long term investment proposals.

questions.text: The time taken to recover the original investment is the
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.explanation: The payback period measures how long the investment takes to repay itself.

questions.text: Net present value is the difference between the present value of cash inflows and the initial investment
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.explanation: NPV discounts all cash flows and subtracts the initial outlay.

questions.text: Explain the importance of capital budgeting
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Capital budgeting involves large irreversible long term commitments that determine the firms future profitability and risk so careful evaluation is essential.
questions.explanation: Cover size irreversibility and long term impact of investment decisions.

questions.text: A project costs 50000 and earns a constant 10000 per year. Its payback period is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.explanation: Payback equals investment divided by annual inflow so 50000 divided by 10000 equals five years.

questions.text: The rate a firm must pay to obtain funds is its
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.explanation: The cost of capital is the minimum return required by suppliers of funds.

questions.text: The mix of debt and equity used to finance a firm is its capital
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.explanation: Capital structure is the proportion of debt and equity financing.

questions.text: Financial leverage is the use of fixed cost debt to magnify returns to shareholders
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.explanation: Leverage uses debt whose fixed interest amplifies both gains and losses.

questions.text: Define cost of capital and its significance
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.correctAnswer: Cost of capital is the minimum return a firm must earn to satisfy its investors and it is used as the discount rate and investment hurdle.
questions.explanation: It is the benchmark for accepting investments.

questions.text: Explain the factors determining capital structure
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.correctAnswer: Capital structure depends on trading on equity tax benefits cost of debt financial risk control considerations and market conditions balancing cheaper debt against the risk of fixed charges.
questions.explanation: Cover the benefits of debt against its financial risk.

questions.text: The management of current assets and current liabilities is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.explanation: Working capital management handles day to day current assets and liabilities.

questions.text: Current assets minus current liabilities equals
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.explanation: Net working capital is the excess of current assets over current liabilities.

questions.text: Excessive working capital is as harmful as inadequate working capital
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.explanation: Too much working capital ties up funds unproductively while too little causes insolvency.

questions.text: List the components of working capital
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.correctAnswer: Cash inventory receivables and short term investments on the asset side and payables on the liability side.
questions.explanation: These current items must be managed for liquidity.

questions.text: Explain the factors determining working capital requirements
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.correctAnswer: Working capital needs depend on the nature of business operating cycle seasonality credit policy inventory turnover and growth. Longer cycles and slower turnover raise the requirement.
questions.explanation: Cover the business and policy factors affecting the level of working capital.

questions.text: If current assets are 80000 and current liabilities are 50000 the net working capital is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.explanation: Net working capital equals current assets minus current liabilities so 80000 minus 50000 equals 30000.

questions.text: The decision on how much profit to distribute to shareholders is the
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.explanation: The dividend decision determines how much earnings are paid out versus retained.

questions.text: A dividend paid in the form of additional shares rather than cash is a
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.explanation: A stock or bonus dividend distributes shares instead of cash.

questions.text: Retained earnings are an internal source of finance
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.explanation: Retained earnings are profits ploughed back making them an internal source.

questions.text: List the sources of long term finance
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.correctAnswer: Equity shares preference shares debentures retained earnings and term loans.
questions.explanation: These provide long term capital for the firm.

questions.text: Explain the theories of dividend policy
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.correctAnswer: The relevance theory argues dividends affect value while the irrelevance theory of Modigliani and Miller holds that value depends only on investment policy under perfect markets.
questions.explanation: Present both the relevance and irrelevance positions.

questions.text: Assertion: Debt is cheaper than equity as a source of finance. Reason: Interest on debt is tax deductible while dividends are not
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure (assertion reason)
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
questions.explanation: The tax shield on interest makes the effective cost of debt lower than equity.

questions.text: Match the decision to its question
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management (matching)
options: Investment decision - where to invest funds
Financing decision - how much profit to pay
Dividend decision - which assets to buy
questions.explanation: The investment decision concerns where to deploy funds.

questions.text: The internal rate of return is the discount rate at which net present value becomes
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.explanation: IRR is the rate that equates the present value of inflows with the outlay.

questions.text: A project with a positive net present value should be accepted
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.explanation: Positive NPV means the project earns more than the cost of capital.

questions.text: Explain the difference between gross and net working capital
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.correctAnswer: Gross working capital is total current assets while net working capital is current assets minus current liabilities.
questions.explanation: Gross focuses on assets while net shows the liquidity cushion.

questions.text: Read the case: A firm must choose between a machine costing 100000 with a five year life and another costing 150000 with a ten year life both with equal annual savings. Which appraisal technique best handles the unequal lives and why
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Net present value with equivalent annual cost comparison is best because the projects have unequal lives and simple NPV comparison is misleading.
questions.explanation: Use equivalent annual cost to compare projects with different lives.

questions.text: Read the case: A firm has high fixed interest charges and faces falling sales. Explain its financial risk and one measure to reduce it
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.correctAnswer: The firm has high financial leverage so falling sales sharply reduce earnings available to shareholders. It should reduce debt and shift toward equity to lower fixed charges.
questions.explanation: Diagnose leverage risk and propose deleveraging.

questions.text: The rate of return that shareholders require on their equity investment is the
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.explanation: The cost of equity is the return demanded by shareholders.

questions.text: Explain the importance of working capital management
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Working capital management
questions.correctAnswer: Working capital management maintains liquidity for day to day operations avoids insolvency and idle funds and supports profitability and creditworthiness.
questions.explanation: Cover liquidity profitability and solvency trade offs.

questions.text: The cost of issuing new securities is called
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.explanation: Flotation costs are underwriting and issue expenses of new securities.

questions.text: Explain the advantages of retained earnings as a source of finance
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.correctAnswer: Retained earnings are an internal source with no issue costs or dilution and are always available. They strengthen the firms capital base and credit standing.
questions.explanation: Cover cost savings no dilution and financial stability.

questions.text: A perpetuity is an annuity that continues forever
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Time value of money and valuation
questions.explanation: A perpetuity pays a fixed amount every period indefinitely.

questions.text: Explain the concept of leverage and its types
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Cost of capital and capital structure
questions.correctAnswer: Leverage is the use of fixed costs to magnify returns. Operating leverage arises from fixed operating costs and financial leverage from fixed interest charges; together they form combined leverage.
questions.explanation: Distinguish operating financial and combined leverage.

questions.text: List the factors affecting the dividend policy of a firm
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.correctAnswer: Earnings liquidity growth opportunities shareholders preferences tax and legal restrictions.
questions.explanation: These factors determine the level of dividend payout.

questions.text: The value of a firm that maximises shareholder wealth is best measured by its share price
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Nature and scope of financial management
questions.explanation: Share price reflects the market value of the firm and thus shareholder wealth.

questions.text: Explain the merits and demerits of the payback period method
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Capital budgeting and investment decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Payback is simple and useful for liquidity and risk screening. Its drawbacks are ignoring the time value of money and the cash flows after the payback period.
questions.explanation: Cover simplicity against the neglect of later flows and timing.

questions.text: A firm pays a dividend of 2 per share on earnings of 8 per share. The payout ratio is
questions.subject: Financial Management
questions.topic: Dividend policy and sources of finance
questions.explanation: Payout ratio equals dividend per share divided by earnings per share so 2 divided by 8 equals 0.25 or twenty five percent.
